title: India Batter Sabbhineni Meghana Announces Retirement From All Forms of Cricket
excerpt: The Andhra Pradesh-born top-order batter ends a career of 3 ODIs and 17 T20Is, a Commonwealth Games silver medal and a 2024 WPL title with Royal Challengers Bengaluru.
body:
• India top-order batter Sabbhineni Meghana announced her retirement from all forms of cricket on Friday, October 23, in a social media post reported by IANS.
  • She represented India in 3 ODIs and 17 T20Is, made her ODI debut against New Zealand on February 12, 2022, and was part of the squad that won silver at the 2022 Commonwealth Games.
  • In the Women's Premier League she played for Gujarat Giants in the inaugural edition and moved to Royal Challengers Bengaluru in 2024, where she was part of the title-winning squad.
  • Meghana said she intends to stay connected to cricket by mentoring the next generation and giving back to the game.

India batter Sabbhineni Meghana has announced her retirement from all forms of cricket. The top-order batter, born in Andhra Pradesh, made the announcement in a social media post on Friday, according to IANS.

"Stepping onto the field for the very first time with a bat in hand to wear a jersey on world stage has been nothing short of a dream come true. As I announce my retirement from all formats of cricket as a player, my heart is overflowing with gratitude."

— Sabbhineni Meghana

An India career in two phases

Meghana represented Railways in domestic cricket after earlier spells with Andhra and South Zone, according to her career record. She made her T20 International debut on November 20, 2016, against West Indies, and was part of India's victorious team at the 2016 Women's Twenty20 Asia Cup. Her One Day International debut came later, on February 12, 2022, against New Zealand.

In total she played 3 ODIs and 17 T20Is for India. Her last T20I was on October 10, 2022, against Thailand at the Women's Asia Cup in Sylhet. In 2022 she was also part of the Indian team that won silver at the Commonwealth Games in Birmingham, where women's T20 cricket featured on the programme.

Domestically, she was the leading run-scorer in the 2021-22 Women's Senior One Day Trophy, with 388 runs including one century and two half-centuries. Her career statistics list a top score of 61 in ODIs and 69 in T20Is.

The WPL chapter

When the Women's Premier League began, Meghana was signed by Gujarat Giants for its inaugural edition. She moved to Royal Challengers Bengaluru in 2024 and was part of the RCB squad that lifted the trophy that season — the closing high point of her playing career reported by IANS.

Since the Commonwealth Games, she had not broken back into India's T20 setup on a regular basis and missed out on subsequent ICC events, IANS reported. That context frames a retirement announced while the memories of a WPL title remain recent.

Gratitude, and what she plans next

In her post, Meghana thanked her family, coaches, teammates and support staff, and thanked the fans whose cheers, she wrote, fuelled every stride she took under the floodlights. She also thanked the BCCI, the Andhra Cricket Association, Royal Challengers Bengaluru, Gujarat Giants and the Railways Sports Promotion Board for their support throughout her career.

"While my playing days come to an end, my bond with cricket will never break. I will always stay deeply connected to the game and intend to dedicate my life to giving back to the sport, mentoring the next generation."

— Sabbhineni Meghana

No further role — in coaching, commentary or administration — was confirmed in the reports of her announcement. What she stated was an intention: to mentor younger players and serve the game that, in her words, gave her everything.
